subject: Post-call recap: throughput & latency constraints — PrimeRetail qualification
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@primeretail.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@primeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: throughput & latency constraints — PrimeRetail qualification

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — I wanted to capture the key items we discussed so the team (and your procurement folks) have a single reference. I also added a proposed next-steps list at the bottom to keep momentum.

Summary of pain & goals (as we heard it):
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference costs during peak promotional windows; current spikes cause timeouts for real-time personalization (~200ms target but frequently >800ms on peak days).
- Business goal: deliver personalized merchandising recommendations with 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for 2000 qps (peak burst), steady-state 500 qps outside promo windows.
- Quality: recommendations must match current model output within a 2% NDCG drop (business tolerance).

Technical constraints & model requirements:
- Models: transformer-based recommendation model (1.2B param dense variant) with short context (max seq 128 tokens). There is a smaller distilled variant (300M) used for cold-starts.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for stateful online requests at 2000 qps burst; desired tail for 99th <= 400ms where possible.
- Throughput SLOs: sustained 500 qps, bursts to 2000 qps for up to 20 minutes during promos.
- Deployment topology: multi-region (us-east primary, us-west DR), preference for Redwood Dedicated with capacity reservation; private VPC option if procurement requires.

Constraints we noted from your infra team:
- Traffic must stay within your VPC for privacy-sensitive payloads.
- KV/cache eviction cannot cause >5ms variability in token generation.
- Encryption requirements: customer-managed KMS for model keys.

Actionable next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood: produce an initial capacity profile and cost estimate for Dedicated pool sized for 2000 qps bursts + autoscale policies (I assigned this to Rishi). Target delivery: 2026-03-30.
2) PrimeRetail: share sample anonymized request traces (1 week) and a small model checkpoint or model signature (weights not required) so we can run a tabletop sizing exercise.
3) Technical deep-dive workshop (60 min) with PrimeRetail infra + model owners and Redwood runtime engineers to validate topology and caching approaches. Tentative date: 2026-04-02.

Attachments: primeretail-inference-topology-v1.pdf (topology sketch) and primeretail-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO table).

If that matches your notes, please reply with any edits to the SLOs or constraints and confirm whether the 4/2 workshop works.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@primeretail.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@primeretail.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & latency constraints — PrimeRetail qualification

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. This aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 2000 qps is expected for a maximum of 15–20 minutes, but it could happen multiple times per day (promo windows).
- The model signature you referenced is a JSON schema and a small tflite export we can share — we will not share full weights until NDA/procurement is in place.
- For the KV/cache note: our current serving layer is using an in-memory Redis cluster; eviction spikes are a known issue in the legacy system.

We can provide a week of anonymized traces by end of day 2026-03-30. The 4/2 workshop is acceptable; Tom and I will plan to attend.

Two asks for Redwood before the workshop:
1) a short (1 page) runbook showing how Redwood Dedicated would handle burst scaling and graceful degradation to a smaller model variant;
2) a preliminary cost-per-1M-request estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated options so procurement can start internal discussions.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jenkins
Director, Personalization Engineering | PrimeRetail
sara.jenkins@primeretail.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Post-call recap: throughput & latency constraints — PrimeRetail qualification

Looping you both in — quick notes from my side after reading the traces Sara offered to provide:

- Size/format constraints: if they can provide 1-minute sampled p95 latency and per-endpoint qps, we can run a tabletop cost model immediately. Full traces help but sampled aggregates are enough for an initial sizing.
- Fast idea: deploy a hybrid topology — Dedicated pool in us-east with an autoscale headroom for bursts, plus a lightweight Hosted fallback in us-west that serves only distilled model for heavy tails (keeps cost predictable).
- KV cache: recommend we propose a two-tier KV solution (local LRU per-serving process + Redis for shared prefix cache) to minimize eviction spikes.

I'll draft the capacity profile and a 1-page runbook for Camila to share (will include degradation strategy and quantization options). Target: EOD 2026-03-30.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & latency constraints — PrimeRetail qualification

Thanks all — appreciated. Quick confirmations and logistics: 

- Rishi will deliver the capacity profile + runbook by 2026-03-30 (will include cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated, autoscale settings, and fallback logic to distilled model).
- Sara: thanks for committing traces — please upload to the shared Drive link in the related_links above (or email to procurement if preferable).
- Workshop confirmed for 2026-04-02 at 10:00 PT — I sent a calendar invite to your team and included an agenda: sizing assumptions, topology options, KV/cache patterns, security/KMS flow, and procurement timeline.

For the workshop please have:
- One infra owner who can speak to VPC peering and KMS requirements.
- One model owner who can walk the model signature and answer questions about acceptable quality deltas for quantization/distillation.

I'll attach the initial topology sketch and SLO matrix to the calendar invite; if there's anything else you want added to the agenda, reply-all and I'll update.

Best regards,
Camila
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
